title: Addressing error and unselected coordinates
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $J$ be a set of coordinates in a cube of dimension $m+2^m$, and let $g$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on that cube which depends only on coordinates in $J$. The sum, over all inputs $x$, of the indicator that $g(x)$ differs from the addressing function is at least half the number of inputs whose selected coordinate is not in $J$.
hypotheses_covered: $J$ is a finite set of coordinates in a cube of dimension $m+2^m$
